discovery: Discovery of baryon acoustic oscillations in the large-scale distribution of galaxies, establishing a standard ruler for cosmic expansion

nominees.name: Daniel J. Eisenstein
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University, Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

nominees.name: Shaun Cole
nominees.affiliation: Durham University, Institute for Computational Cosmology, UK

nominees.name: Matthew Colless
nominees.affiliation: Australian National University, Research School of Astronomy and Astrophysics, Australia

motivation: In 2005 the SDSS (Eisenstein et al.) and 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey (Cole et al.) independently detected the baryon acoustic oscillation feature in galaxy clustering: the imprint, frozen into matter at recombination, of sound waves in the primordial photon-baryon plasma. Eisenstein developed the theory that made the feature a precise standard ruler and led its detection; Cole led the 2dFGRS power-spectrum measurement; Colless co-led the 2dFGRS survey that made it possible. The discovery confirmed that cosmic structure grew gravitationally from the same fluctuations seen in the microwave background, with cold dark matter dominating the mass. It created a geometric probe of the expansion history, independent of supernovae, that underpins BOSS, eBOSS and DESI. DESI's 2024-25 BAO results, which hint that dark energy may evolve with time, show that this tool now bears on fundamental physics.
